subject: English
title: Year 7 English: Half-term 5 (Non-fiction: purpose and persuasion)

questions.question:
Read the passage.

"Every year, over 8 million tonnes of plastic enter our oceans. That is a rubbish truck full of plastic every single minute. Turtles mistake bags for jellyfish. Seabirds feed bottle tops to their chicks. But you can help. Carry a reusable bottle. Say no to straws. Small changes, made by millions of us, add up to a cleaner sea. Start today."

What is the main purpose of this text?
options: To persuade readers to reduce plastic use
To explain how plastic is made
questions.answer: To persuade readers to reduce plastic use
questions.explanation: It uses facts and commands to get readers to act.

"That is a rubbish truck full of plastic every single minute." Why does the writer include this?
options: To make the big number easy to picture
questions.answer: To make the big number easy to picture
questions.explanation: Turning 8 million tonnes into a familiar image makes the scale shocking.

questions.explanation: Carry and Say are commands telling the reader what to do.

Why does the writer mention turtles and seabirds?
options: To appeal to the reader's emotions
To show the writer is a vet
questions.answer: To appeal to the reader's emotions
questions.explanation: Harm to animals makes readers feel sympathy, so they are more likely to act.

questions.question: Which of these is an opinion?
options: Water boils at 100°C at sea level.
London is the capital of the UK.
There are seven days in a week.
Football is the best sport in the world.
questions.answer: Football is the best sport in the world.
questions.explanation: 'Best' is a judgement that people can disagree with.

questions.question: Which feature would you expect in a newspaper report?
options: A headline and quotes from witnesses
questions.answer: A headline and quotes from witnesses
questions.explanation: Reports use headlines, facts and quotes.

questions.question: Which opening suits a formal letter to a headteacher?
questions.explanation: 'Dear Mr Patel,' is formal and polite.

questions.question: r"Don't you want a safer town?" What technique is this?
questions.explanation: A question that doesn't need an answer, used to make the reader agree.

questions.question: Which phrase uses the 'rule of three'?
questions.explanation: Three items in a list sound complete and memorable.

questions.question: Which text is mainly written to inform?
questions.explanation: Bus times give information; the advert persuades and the story entertains.
